title: Sora 2
hook: OpenAI's Sora 2 added synchronized audio and sharper physical consistency — and shipped inside a TikTok-style social app where you remix each other's generations.
key_points: OpenAI's video-and-audio model, released September 2025 as the successor to Sora.
Generates synchronized speech, sound effects, and ambient audio with the video.
Improved physical realism and consistency over the original Sora.
Launched with a social iOS app for creating, remixing, and 'cameo' insertion of people.
content_html: OpenAI released Sora 2 in September 2025, the next generation of its text-to-video system, and — unusually — wrapped it in a consumer social app. Like Google's Veo 3, Sora 2 generates synchronized audio together with the video, and it improved the physical consistency that made the first Sora's demos occasionally surreal.
extra_html:
What's new

Sora 2 produces clips with matching speech, Foley-style sound effects, and ambient audio, and handles motion and physics more believably than its predecessor. OpenAI launched it alongside a social iOS app called Sora, where users create videos, remix each other's generations in a feed, and insert themselves or friends into clips via a "cameo" feature — a deliberate push to make generative video a participatory, social product rather than a pro tool.

Why it matters

Two things stand out. Technically, joint audio-video generation with better physics moved AI video toward finished content. Strategically, shipping it as a social app — rather than just an API — was a bet that the killer use of generative video is consumer creation and remixing, raising fresh questions about likeness, consent, and provenance that the cameo feature made concrete.

related.title: Sora: Video Generation as World Simulation
related.hook: OpenAI's Sora generates minute-long high-fidelity video from text by treating video as space-time patches - and frames the whole task as learning a world simulator.

related.title: Veo 3
related.hook: Google's Veo 3 generates video with synchronized native audio — dialogue, sound effects, and ambient noise produced together with the picture, not dubbed on after.

flashcards.prompt: What were the two main advances of Sora 2 over the original Sora?
flashcards.back_html: Synchronized audio (speech, sound effects, ambient sound) generated with the video, plus improved physical realism and consistency.

flashcards.prompt: Why was shipping Sora 2 inside a social iOS app strategically notable?

choices.text: It bet the killer use of generative video is consumer creation and remixing
It was meant only for professional film studios
It abandoned the underlying video model entirely

flashcards.explanation_html: Launching as a social app, not just an API, was a bet on participatory consumer creation and remixing — raising questions about likeness and consent via the cameo feature.
